A1.justification: Both PDFs describe M3KG-RAG and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and nine supplementary pages covering Appendices A-D. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA evaluations, baseline comparisons, ablations, sensitivity analyses, computational costs, and qualitative examples in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1-4 and 15 and the supplementary sensitivity and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The graph-construction agents, modality-wise retrieval, GRASP grounding/filtering, and graph-augmented generation remain unchanged. The benchmark-specific threshold revision concerns an experimental setting; correcting 'Grounding' to 'Grounded' does not introduce a component.

E1.justification: Both versions construct graphs from AudioCaps, ActivityNet, and VALOR and evaluate AudioCaps-QA, VCGPT, and VALOR. No datasets, tasks, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 retain None, Wikidata, VTKG, M2ConceptBase, and VAT-KG. The GPT-4o comparison in Table 3 retains None and VAT-KG, and supplementary comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported AudioCaps-QA retrieval-distance threshold τ from 0.3 to 3.0. Other settings and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. This is a definite reported setting revision, but neither PDF establishes whether experiments were rerun or a reporting error was corrected.

E4.justification: The modality-wise retrieval/GRASP ablation, threshold sensitivity study, GRASP component and computational-cost analysis, and qualitative cases are retained unchanged in Table 4, Appendix B, and Figures 4-8.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same point scores and preference rates without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported scores, preference rates, resource measurements, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including Tables 1-4 and 15 and Figures 4-8. No revised outcomes accompany the AudioCaps-QA threshold change.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6, the graph-coverage property, and the supplementary threshold definitions remain unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about multi-hop graph construction, modality-wise retrieval, GRASP, and improved multimodal reasoning. The added project link does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of retrieval, grounding, pruning, and empirical results remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same limitations concerning corpus coverage and dependence on encoders and grounding models.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-site link, revises the documented AudioCaps-QA threshold, and adds acknowledgements mentioning NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q support. The single-H100 experimental statement and supplementary implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish what resources the website provides.

R1.justification: The same 58 references and related-work positioning are retained. Bibliography entries move because acknowledgements were inserted, without changes to cited works or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations, standardizes one GRASP expansion, corrects AudioCaps-QA capitalization, and adds a project-site sentence and acknowledgements. The scientific narrative and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added link and acknowledgements cause local layout changes and bibliography reflow; Table 3's dataset header capitalization is corrected. Figures and table structures are retained, and all supplementary pages render identically.

improvement.justification: The project-site pointer, support disclosures, and terminology corrections modestly improve documentation and consistency. Methods, evidence, and appendices remain unchanged. The unexplained threshold revision cannot be credited as an experimental improvement or a verified reproducibility correction, limiting the demonstrated gains to documentation.
